To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DOC pool in a regional confined aquifer is controlled by a combination of in-situ and external sources.

(i) soil zone and organic rich sediments are the primary sources of DOC in the aquifer, (ii) soil zone is more important in recharge areas and organic rich sedments in the central part, (iii) DOC in the aquifers is not derived from bedrock.
the DOC pool in a regional confined groundwater flow system is controlled by a combination of in situ organic matter and DOC from soil zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the chemical and isotopic composition of DOC in groundwater is controlled by the interaction of DOC sources and processes in the aquifer.
the origin of the DOC pool in a regional confined aquifer and its relation to the CH4 production.
the DOC cycle of the regional confined methanogenesis aquifer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DOC is derived from a combination of soil zone and in-situ sources.
the DOC in the aquifer is a mixture of terrestrial organic matter from the soil zone and the aquifer matrix.
soil and organic rich sediments are the major DOC sources in the studied aquifer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DOC cycle in the regional groundwater system is controlled by the interaction between the organic carbon source and the hydrogeological conditions.
the DOC cycle is driven by two main sources, a soil-derived DOC and an in situ DOC source.
in a confined aquifer with a regional flow system, soil zone and in-situ organic rich sediments in the aquifer are the primary sources of DOC in groundwater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DOC in groundwater is not only a mixture of terrestrial and bedrock-derived organic matter, but also a mixture of different terrestrial organic matter fractions.
a combined use of DOC and CH4 carbon isotopic data is an excellent way to understand the carbon dynamics of regional confined aquifers.
the combined use of chemical (DOC concentration) and isotopic (14C and 13C-NMRS) tools provides a better insight on the DOC cycle in groundwater than a single approach.
